known_errors.title: Resolvent absolute continuity is overstated from mu-a.e. to every initial condition

<verdict>INCORRECT</verdict>
<error_description>
The proof fails at the step “The assumed uniqueness in law of the ABLM mild solution therefore identifies this resolvent with the resolvent of \(P_t\).” The external ABLM uniqueness result does not apply to the present Dirichlet-boundary setting. In ABLM, the main setup covers only \(D=\mathbb R\), \([0,1]\) with periodic boundary conditions, or \([0,1]\) with Neumann boundary conditions, and the paper explicitly says that it does not analyze equation (1.1) with Dirichlet boundary conditions. The present Assertion is explicitly the Dirichlet stochastic heat equation on \([0,1]\), with \(E=C_0([0,1])\), the Brownian bridge reference law, and the Dirichlet Laplacian. Thus the domain/boundary-condition hypothesis needed to invoke ABLM uniqueness is not satisfied. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2011.13498))

This is load-bearing: BZ14 Proposition 2.5 gives absolute continuity for the resolvent of the Dirichlet-form semigroup/process in their setting, but the proof still needs a valid identification of that resolvent with the pointwise resolvent \(\mathcal R_\alpha(x,\cdot)\) of the asserted semigroup \(P_t\) for every \(x\in E\). The proposed identification is made through an external uniqueness theorem whose hypotheses fail here. Moreover, the cited Established Result “Lemma 5.2” states that \(P_t\) is the Markov semigroup associated with the closed form; it does not, as stated, supply an ABLM Dirichlet-boundary uniqueness theorem or an equivalence between BZ’s local-time weak formulation and the ABLM mild formulation for Dirichlet boundary conditions.
</error_description>
